newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 9.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Thursday:
- The Irish government is fearful of a collapse in the beef market following news that the Russians are seeking an extension of their partial ban on Irish beef.
- Unemployment had fallen to its lowest level in five years with official figures showing a drop of 15,300 in the live register at the end of 1996 to 267,000.
- Investment intermediaries will have to comply with a more demanding regulatory regime under the supervision of the central bank, according to its governor, Maurice O'Connell.

- Dixons, the British electronic goods giant, plans to take over the Harry Moore chain by the end of the month but will continue to use the Irish firm's brand name and will retain most its staff, industry sources said.
- Irish agriculture faced a major new crisis last night after it emerged that Russia is demanding the banning of beef from a further five counties because of BSE.
- The battle to supply Ireland's local radio stations and their 1.4 million listeners with a national news service has intensified.
- Fundamental problems exist with the planned legislation to regulate investment brokers in the wake of the Tony Taylor affair, central bank governor Maurice O'Connell said.
- Kevin Keegan resigned as manager of Newcastle United yesterday after banks forced his hand to allow the club's 150 million pound stock market flotation to go ahead smoothly.
